line: Copper worked in these hills long before anyone wanted the silver beneath it.
A tyrant's holding. **Peisistratos** drew revenue from the mines before the city did.
A single rich strike. **Themistokles** argued the windfall into two hundred ships instead of a dividend.
The mines stopped. **Sparta** held **Dekeleia** year-round and twenty thousand slaves walked out.
A **Mycenaean** citadel on the rock, walled while the palaces elsewhere burned.
**Solon** cancelled the debts and wrote law that outlasted him.
The **Peisistratid** century. A tyranny that built, and paid for it out of **Laureion**.
**Kleisthenes** cut the citizen body into demes and made the tribes artificial on purpose.
Burned by the **Persians**. The city was evacuated to **Salamis** and came back to ash.
The **Parthenon** raised on the burnt foundations, out of the tribute of the empire.
Twenty-seven years of war, and a plague in the second summer that killed a third of the city.
**Sokrates** tried and condemned by a jury of five hundred and one.
**Chaeronea**. **Philip** ended the independence of the Greek cities on a plain in **Boeotia**.
**Sulla** stormed the walls and sacked the city that had backed **Mithridates**.
The **Herulian** sack. The city withdrew behind a smaller wall built of its own rubble.
A **Venetian** shell found the powder the **Ottomans** stored in the **Parthenon**.
The bull of **Marathon**, which **Theseus** took before he went to **Crete**.
**Peisistratos** came ashore here to take **Athens** for the third time.
The **Persians** landed on this beach and the **Athenians** held the high edge of the plain.
Palaces at **Knossos** and **Phaistos**, and a sea power with no walls.
The labyrinth and the tribute of youths — the story **Athens** told about **Crete**.
**Aristotle** read the **Cretan** constitution as the model **Sparta** copied.
Taken by **Rome** in three campaigns and made a province with **Cyrene**.
